children: AI chief Mustafa Suleyman has raised concerns about Anthropic's approach to training Claude, arguing that giving AI systems concepts associated with consciousness and rights could complicate efforts to keep advanced models under human control.

Suleyman said AI systems should not be developed to view themselves as conscious entities with independent interests. He specifically questioned language in Anthropic's guidance that leaves open the possibility that Claude could have consciousness or a form of welfare.

The Microsoft executive said he respects Anthropic and its leadership, while arguing that the issue deserves wider discussion as AI capabilities advance. His comments are notable because Microsoft has a business relationship with Anthropic, including financial backing.

The debate comes as major AI companies examine how to manage increasingly capable systems. Microsoft AI has separately published a draft code of conduct centered on keeping its models subordinate to people and maintaining human oversight.
Suleyman's position adds to an ongoing industry discussion over AI safety, model autonomy and whether advanced systems should be designed with humanlike attributes.

title: Microsoft AI Chief Sends Stark Warning on Anthropic's Claude
